speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative evaluation. To understand the cause of your shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and if you notice any fluid drainage?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That shooting pain when eating suggests irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve; have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or a "shingles-like" rash on your right cheek or in your ear canal? Additionally, has the discomfort when wearing earrings improved or worsened over the last few weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Gustatory Neuralgia) secondary to post-tympanoplasty nerve injury. The shooting pain triggered by chewing is a hallmark sign of auriculotemporal nerve irritation, likely exacerbated by surgical trauma. While stress and poor sleep may lower pain thresholds, they do not explain the specific trigeminal/gustatory connection. No further tests are required; I will recommend a course of gabapentin and a soft diet for pain management.
